paragraphs: Alivia Analytics sells software and services that help health plans and government agencies cut the losses caused by fraud, waste, abuse and payment errors. Its platform, Alivia 360, gathers pre-payment and post-payment work into one suite.

Before a claim is paid, a claims manager scores high-risk providers and applies configurable pend-and-review triggers with compliance checks. After payment, a lead-finding tool feeds special investigations units while a case manager handles the volume of cases and the workflow around them. A separate data service standardizes claims data into analytics-ready formats and takes in whatever the payer sends. The company frames its AI as an assistant rather than a replacement, with human oversight and ethical use.

Buyers span Medicaid, Medicare and state programs as well as private health plans, third party administrators and self-insured employers. The company says it began by helping state Medicaid programs and Blues organizations speed up post-pay recoveries. A leadership page lists a full slate of officers, among them a chief information security officer.
